transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen, Devon Patel, Lina Torres, Ethan Brooks (Redwood); Alex Rivera, Priya Shah, Sam Gold, Marta Iglesias, Toby Lee, Jordan Kim (Halo Systems)

Summary: Brief onboarding kickoff primarily run by Redwood CSM/AE to align scope for a short Dedicated pilot, identify security/network prerequisites for Private/Dedicated deployment, and agree next steps for an infra deep dive. Conversation touched on latency targets, data residency, KMS, and integration timeline. Transcription is automated and contains minor errors.

[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood): Alright hey everyone thanks for joining, I'll do a quick roll call and then we can get into the kickoff agenda. Appreciate you carving out time.
[00:00:15] Alex (Halo): Hi all, Alex here — excited to get started.
[00:00:18] Priya (Halo): Priya from infra — hi.
[00:00:00] Sam (Halo): Sam, product.
[00:00:30] Maya (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: success criteria, pilot scope, security/network checklist, who owns what, and scheduling the infra deep dive. Lina will run the CSM pieces, Devon and Ethan handle the technical bits.
[00:00:42] Lina (Redwood): Hi everyone — we'll aim to keep this tight at 45 minutes but leave time for questions.

[00:01:10] Alex (Halo): To set context: Halo's use case is an in-app assistant for enterprise customers — we'll serve conversations and embeddings for search and personalization. Latency is important for the chat interactions — ideally p95 under 250 ms for short responses, but we can be flexible during pilot.
[00:01:32] Devon (Redwood): Got it. Quick clarifying q: are you planning to use hosted first and then move to private/dedicated, or go straight to a VPC/private deployment?
[00:01:43] Alex (Halo): We're looking to evaluate Dedicated capacity first because of throughput needs and data locality, but want the option to run a private control plane later for compliance.
[00:02:05] Priya (Halo): Security team will want KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO mapping to our IdP — SAML. We also have data residency constraints for EU customers.
[00:02:15] Marta (Halo): SOC2 and ISO27001 evidence, plus any penetration test artifacts.
[00:02:20] Lina (Redwood): That's expected. We'll share our security pack and SOC2 summary; Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and SAML SSO, and we have audit logs retention options.

[00:03:00] Devon (Redwood): For the Dedicated pilot, a few notes: we'll provision a small GPU pool that matches your traffic profile, and we'll instrument observability endpoints so you can see token-level cost and p95 latency. During the pilot we can enable aggressive prefix caching to reduce token spend.
[00:03:20] Jordan (Halo): When you say token-level cost — can we get CSV dumps or is it only in the console?
[00:03:27] Ethan (Redwood): Both. We can push usage exports to an S3 bucket on a cadence, and you can also view per-route dashboards.

[00:04:10] Sam (Halo): About model versions — we have a preference for an open model with tuned safety layers. Do you have a recommended model for search embeddings vs chat?
[00:04:20] Devon (Redwood): Typically for embeddings we suggest the x-embed-1 series (example), and for chat we can suggest a 7B-13B variant depending on quality vs latency tradeoffs; we can run a quick quality baseline on your few prompt sets.
[00:04:35] Alex (Halo): We'll provide sample prompts and benchmark dataset.

[00:05:15] Priya (Halo): Networking — VPC peering is our preferred option. We need to know firewall IPs, egress ports, and whether you need a NAT. Also what encryption in transit expectations are.
[00:05:30] Ethan (Redwood): For Dedicated/VPC we do peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your infra. We'll share the egress list — generally TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS options for Private deployments. For hosted there's encrypted in transit with customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest on Private.

[00:06:00] Toby (Halo): Follow-up: do you require inbound rules or is the connection outbound from our VPC?
[00:06:08] Devon (Redwood): Usually outbound from your VPC to our dedicated endpoints; if you want fully private on-prem, we can flip to a customer managed control plane — that's a longer setup.

[00:06:55] Alex (Halo): Timeline: we want to run a 2-week pilot starting June 2 to evaluate latency and cost. After pilot we'll decide on expansion to a monthly reserved Dedicated contract.
[00:07:05] Maya (Redwood): That timeline works on our side. Key milestones: preflight checks and infra readiness this week, pilot provisioning the week of June 2, and a mid-pilot review after 7 days.

[00:07:40] Sam (Halo): Who should own the preflight checklist on Redwood side?
[00:07:43] Lina (Redwood): I'll own the checklist and invite Halo to the customer workspace. Devon and Ethan will run the infra checks.

[00:08:20] Alex (Halo): A couple of product constraints: we have rate-limited downstream APIs and want graceful degradation. Does Redwood support fallback to smaller models (cost tier) automatically?
[00:08:32] Devon (Redwood): Yes — smart routing policies let you route by latency or cost and fallback to compatible model variants. We can configure automatic fallback rules during the pilot.

[00:09:05] Priya (Halo): On telemetry: will logs include raw prompts? We have PII restrictions — ideally redaction prior to logs.
[00:09:14] Lina (Redwood): We have config to redact or hash prompt contents in audit logs; plus you can opt for minimal logging in pilot. We'll include that in the runbook.

[00:10:00] Jordan (Halo): For embeddings batch jobs we plan to backfill 50M docs over time. Any guidance on throughput and cost optimization?
[00:10:12] Devon (Redwood): We'll advise batch parallelism and quantized model options for embeddings; also keep an eye on caching and chunking heuristics. We can run a small sample job during pilot to estimate costs.

[00:11:05] Marta (Halo): Security Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM attestation?
[00:11:10] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, we support KMS integrations with CMK; HSM attestation depends on private deployment options, we'll follow up with specifics.

[00:12:00] Sam (Halo): Are there known limitations with response streaming for long outputs? We want streaming for UX.
[00:12:10] Devon (Redwood): We support streaming responses and function/tool calling. Streaming performance depends on network topology; we'll test streaming in your environment.

[00:13:00] Alex (Halo): Pricing: give us a rough idea for Dedicated trial; don't need exact numbers but ballpark so procurement can plan.
[00:13:08] Maya (Redwood): We'll share a summarized pricing deck — for trial we often provide short-term reserved capacity discounts; I'll include the trial pricing options in the docs we send.

[00:14:30] Priya (Halo): On compliance, we need a list of subprocessors and data flow diagrams.
[00:14:38] Lina (Redwood): We'll include subprocessor list and a high-level data flow diagram in the security pack. If you need detailed diagrams for legal, we can generate those with your infra specifics.

[00:15:20] Jordan (Halo): One technical deep dive item: KV cache behavior for multi-tenant prompts. How are cache keys scoped?
[00:15:30] Devon (Redwood): KV cache is tenant-scoped by default; we can also enable prefix caching per user session to improve latency on repeated contexts. We'll share a short doc on cache semantics.

[00:16:45] Alex (Halo): Who is the day-to-day contact for pilot issues?
[00:16:50] Lina (Redwood): That will be me as CSM; Maya is the AE for commercial, Devon and Ethan for technical. We'll set up a Slack channel for rapid triage.

[00:18:00] Sam (Halo): Good. Regarding success criteria: our internal bar is p95 latency under 300 ms for chat, embedding QPS of X, and cost per 1k tokens under Y — we'll formalize and send these numbers.
[00:18:12] Maya (Redwood): Perfect — please send the thresholds and we'll add them to the pilot SLAs.

[00:19:10] Priya (Halo): A note on data residency: our EU customer subset must be served from eu-west-1 or an EU region. Can Dedicated be pinned to a region?
[00:19:20] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated capacity can be region-pinned; Private deployments are also an option for stricter residency.

[00:20:05] Alex (Halo): A quick question on routing: if a model update causes quality regressions, can we rollback automatically?
[00:20:12] Devon (Redwood): Rollouts support canary and automatic rollback policies tied to eval sets. We'll hook your prompt-set evaluations so regressions trigger alerts and rollbacks.

[00:21:30] Jordan (Halo): For trial provisioning, what are the credentials and access patterns? Will we get API keys per environment?
[00:21:38] Ethan (Redwood): Yes — we'll provide scoped API keys per environment (dev/stage/prod) and you can manage them in Console with RBAC.

[00:23:00] Sam (Halo): Do you have reference architectures for common setups (SaaS multi-tenant + embeddings + streaming)?
[00:23:08] Lina (Redwood): Yes — we have a repo of reference architectures and we've got a tailored doc for SaaS patterns; we'll share the link.

[00:24:50] Alex (Halo): Anything in the pilot we should avoid — I mean, are there gotchas?
[00:24:58] Devon (Redwood): Biggest gotchas are long streaming sessions that increase KV resident set sizes and unmanaged backfills that spike token usage. We'll advise safe parallelism and cache TTLs to avoid surprises.

[00:25:40] Priya (Halo): On the legal route: procurement will want indemnity language and DPA clauses — should we loop legal now or after pilot?
[00:25:50] Maya (Redwood): It's fine to loop legal early for redlines; we'll share our standard DPA and we can start that thread if you prefer.

[00:26:55] Jordan (Halo): Could you share a quick checklist of infra items we need to complete before provisioning?
[00:27:02] Lina (Redwood): Yes — the preflight includes: confirm VPC peering/private link, open egress ports, prepare S3 bucket for usage exports, provide IdP SAML metadata, and share KMS contact. I'll post the checklist after this call.

[00:28:30] Marta (Halo): Also please include pen test schedule and any SOC2 attestations timeline.
[00:28:36] Lina (Redwood): Will do.

[00:29:50] Maya (Redwood): Ok I'm going to recap next steps and owners: Lina will send the onboarding playbook and preflight checklist (action: Lina); Devon will assemble model recommendation and sample eval plan (action: Devon); Ethan will send VPC/IP ranges and private deployment options (action: Ethan); Halo to share prompt sets, target SLAs, and contact for KMS (action: Halo).

[00:31:00] Alex (Halo): We can have the prompt sets and SLA targets by Friday.
[00:31:08] Priya (Halo): We'll get firewall egress lists to Toby — Toby will share with Redwood by Thursday.

[00:32:12] Sam (Halo): Question on monitoring: can we plug in our Datadog or do you provide traces?
[00:32:20] Devon (Redwood): We emit tracing hooks and metrics; you can pull those into Datadog or we can set up direct exporter.

[00:33:40] Jordan (Halo): Another item: rate limits and quota — we want bumping thresholds for the pilot, is that possible?
[00:33:48] Ethan (Redwood): Yes we can temporarily raise quotas for pilot; we'll capture the expected QPS in the provisioning ticket.

[00:35:00] Priya (Halo): Any special networking for on-prem nodes if we decide Private later?
[00:35:08] Devon (Redwood): On-prem requires a different control plane topology — more manual setup and likely an air-gapped package; timeline is usually longer. We'll document that path separately.

[00:36:10] Alex (Halo): Competition: we've spoken to Anthropic and Google Vertex; main differentiator for us is clear telemetry and predictable costs.
[00:36:20] Maya (Redwood): Noted — we'll highlight the token-level cost dashboards and rollout controls in the materials we send.

[00:37:45] Sam (Halo): Any immediate blockers we should know of?
[00:37:50] Toby (Halo): For us firewall and IdP metadata are blockers — once we share those we can proceed.

[00:38:30] Lina (Redwood): We'll send the playbook and invite you to the CSM workspace within 24 hours.

[00:39:05] Maya (Redwood): Scheduling: let's book the infra deep dive for the week of May 26 — does Tuesday 14:00 UTC work?
[00:39:16] Priya (Halo): Tuesday works.
[00:39:20] Alex (Halo): Confirm.

[00:40:00] Maya (Redwood): Great. Any final questions?
[00:40:10] Alex (Halo): One last item — will you provide an SLO doc for the pilot?
[00:40:16] Devon (Redwood): Yes we'll draft an SLO tied to your thresholds and include rollback criteria.

[00:41:05] Sam (Halo): Sounds good.
[00:41:20] Priya (Halo): Thanks, appreciate the details.

[00:42:00] Maya (Redwood): Okay we'll stop there — recap in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
